'''Gheorghe Călugăreanu''' (16 June 1902 – 15 November 1976) was a Romanian mathematician, professor at [[Babeș-Bolyai University]], and full member of the [[Romanian Academy]].

He was born in [[Iași]], the son of physician, naturalist, and physiologist [[Dimitrie Călugăreanu]]. From 1913 to 1921 he studied at the [[Gheorghe Lazăr National College, Bucharest|Gheorghe Lazăr High School]] in [[Bucharest]], after which he attended [[Babeș-Bolyai University|University of Cluj]], graduating in 1924. In 1926 he went to [[Paris]] to pursue his studies at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]], supported by a scholarship from the Romanian government.<ref name="Mac">{{MacTutor|id=Calugareanu}}</ref> He obtained his Ph.D. in mathematics in 1929, with thesis ''Sur les fonctions polygènes d'une variable complexe'' written under the direction of [[Émile Picard]]<ref name="Mac"/><ref name="MG">{{MathGenealogy|id=138132}}</ref> and defended before a jury that also included [[Édouard Goursat]] and [[Gaston Julia]].<ref>{{cite thesis|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/THESE_1928__91__1_0.pdf|title=Sur les fonctions polygènes d'une variable complexe|first=Georges|last=Calugaréano|year=1928|publisher=Gauthier-Villars et Cie|location=Paris|series=Thèses de sciences|mr=3532954|jfm=54.0375.03|oclc=459041833}}</ref> After returning to Romania, he was  appointed assistant the University of Cluj in 1930; he was promoted to lecturer in 1934 and named professor in 1942. From 1953 to 1957 he served as Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics.<ref name="Mac"/><ref name="Cluj">{{cite web|url=https://www.cs.ubbcluj.ro/profesor-gheorghe-calugareanu/|title=Profesor Gheorghe Călugareanu|lang=ro|first1=Petru T. |last1=Mocanu|author-link1=Petru Mocanu| first2=Grigore|last2=Sălăgean|access-date=August 19, 2022}}</ref> His Ph.D. students include [[Petru Mocanu]].<ref name="MG"/> He was elected a corresponding member of the Romanian Academy in 1955, and he became a full member in 1963.<ref name="ictp"/>

Călugăreanu studied the theory of [[functions of a complex variable]] ([[meromorphic function]]s, [[univalent function]]s, [[analytic extension]] invariants), as well as [[differential geometry]] and [[algebraic topology]], especially in [[knot theory]]. In his best-known work,<ref name="Călugăreanu1961">{{cite journal|first=Gheorghe|last=Călugăreanu|title=Sur les classes d'isotopie des nœuds tridimensionnels et leurs invariants|lang=fr|journal=Czechoslovak Mathematical Journal |volume=11 |year=1961|issue=4|pages=588–625|mr=0149378|doi=10.21136/CMJ.1961.100486|doi-access=free}}</ref> he established in 1961 the following foundational result regarding the [[writhe]] of a [[Knot (mathematics)|knot]]: take a [[Ribbon (mathematics)|ribbon]] in [[three-dimensional space]], let <math>\operatorname{Lk}</math> be the [[linking number]] of its border components, and let <math>\operatorname{Tw}</math> be its total [[Twist (differential geometry)|twist]]; then the difference <math>\operatorname{Wr}=\operatorname{Lk}-\operatorname{Tw}</math> depends only on the core curve of the ribbon.<ref name="Cimasoni">{{cite journal|last=Cimasoni|first=David|title=Computing the writhe of a knot|journal=[[Journal of Knot Theory and Its Ramifications]]| year=2001|volume=10|issue=387|pages=387–395|mr=1825964| doi=10.1142/S0218216501000913|arxiv=math/0406148|s2cid=15850269}}</ref> In a  paper from 1959,<ref name="Călugăreanu1959">{{cite journal|first=Gheorghe|last=Călugăreanu|title=L'intégrale de Gauss et l'analyse des nœuds tridimensionnels|lang=fr|journal=Revue de Mathématiques Pure et Appliquées |volume=4 |year=1959|pages=5–20|mr=0131846|url=http://math.ubbcluj.ro/~calu/59gauss.pdf}}</ref> he showed how to calculate the writhe of a knot by means of a Gaussian [[multiple integral|double integral]].<ref>{{cite journal|first=Gheorghe|last=Vrănceanu|author-link=Gheorghe Vrănceanu|title=On a geometrical interpretation of Călugăreanu's invariant| journal=Revue Roumaine de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées |volume=17 |year=1972|pages= 1481–1486|mr=0324602}}</ref> Călugăreanu's formula has since been pursued by James H. White<ref>{{cite journal |last=White |first=James H. |title=Self-linking and the Gauss integral in higher dimensions |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=91 |issue=3 |pages=693–728 |year=1969 |doi=10.2307/2373348 |jstor=2373348 |mr=0253264}}</ref> and F. Brock Fuller,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Fuller|first=F. Brock|title=The writhing number of a space curve|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]|year=1971|volume=68|issue=4|pages=815–819|doi=10.1073/pnas.68.4.815|mr=0278197|pmid=5279522|pmc=389050|bibcode=1971PNAS...68..815B|doi-access=free}}</ref> leading to applications in [[Nucleic acid structure|DNA topology]], where writhe is used to describe the amount a piece of [[DNA]] is deformed as a result of [[Torsion (mechanics)|torsional]] stress (a phenomenon known as [[DNA supercoil]]ing).<ref>{{cite book|last1=Bates|first1=Andrew D.|first2=Anthony|last2= Maxwell |title=DNA Topology|year=2005|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |edition=2nd|location=Oxford |isbn=978-0-19-850655-3|pages=36–37|url=http://ukcatalogue.oup.com/product/9780198506553.do#.USxMzKWfOlk|oclc=64239232}}</ref> The topological interpretation of [[Helicity (particle physics)|helicity]] in terms of the Gauss linking number and its limiting form has been called the "Călugăreanu invariant" by [[Keith Moffatt]] and [[Renzo L. Ricca]].<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=Henry Keith|last1= Moffatt|author1-link=Keith Moffatt|first2=Renzo L.|last2= Ricca|author2-link=Renzo L. Ricca|year=1992 |title=Helicity and the Călugăreanu invariant |journal=[[Proceedings of the Royal Society|Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A. Mathematical and Physical Sciences]] |volume=439 |issue=1906 |pages=411–429 |doi=10.1098/rspa.1992.0159 |jstor=52228|bibcode= 1992RSPSA.439..411M|hdl= 10281/20227|mr=1193010|s2cid= 122310895|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

He died of cancer in [[Cluj-Napoca]] in 1976; following his wishes, he was cremated and the urn was deposited at [[Bellu Cemetery]] in Bucharest.<ref name="ictp">{{cite web|url=https://ictp.acad.ro/gheorghe-calugareanu/|title=Gheorghe Călugăreanu (1902–1976). Life and Work|publisher=[[Tiberiu Popoviciu Institute of Numerical Analysis]]|website=ictp.acad.ro|access-date=August 18, 2022}}</ref>
